text.p: * Analysts say sterling eyeing upside vs German mark but strong resistance looms from congestion during last three weeks' trading. Consolidation expected against the dollar.

* After breaking resistance at Friday's high of 2.9494 marks, pound looks set for possible assault on the 2.9650/30 area. This is a 38.2 percent retracement from the multi-year high at 3.0878 on July 28 and the Aug 18 trough at 2.8857. Beyond that, strong congestion around 2.9760.
* Fair congestive support at last Tuesday's low of 2.9330 and then Friday's low of 2.9220.
* Cable looks consolidating in range between 1.60 and 1.6170, analysts said.

* Pound looks held strongly at 1.6170, which 38.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the move from 1.6986 on July 11 to 1.5662 on Aug 8. A breakthrough of this level would allow sterling back to 1.6320.
* Psychologcal prop at $1.60 and strong support in $1.5930 and 1.5940 area which heavily traded in last weeks.
Sterling was eyeing the upside on the German mark on Tuesday but looked set to consolidate over the day in a relatively narrow band against the dollar, technical analysts said.
"The cable upmove still looks pretty much corrective," Mark Ostwald of Monument Derivatives said. "I don't know if we're going to get any new lows for quite a while."
After breaking below the psychological $1.60 barrier, the pound would meet what Ostwald called "enormous support" in a congestive area between 1.5930 and 1.5940, around the highs of last week.
